articles.title: Two Vietnamese students won nearly 1 billion VND scholarships from New Zealand
articles.summary: Two Vietnamese students have been awarded a scholarship package worth nearly 1 billion VND from the New Zealand Government and New Zealand universities. This marks the first time such a scholarship package has been awarded to students from Vietnam.
articles.insight:
This news signals growing Vietnamese student interest in high-value, government-backed scholarships in English-speaking destinations, potentially reflecting shifting preferences toward affordability and prestige—though it remains unclear whether this reflects broader demand shifts or isolated high-achiever outcomes.  
Admissions teams should monitor Vietnamese application volumes, scholarship uptake rates, and social media sentiment around New Zealand’s recent outreach, while reviewing their own merit-based funding visibility and regional partnership strategies to remain competitive.

articles.title: Capes scholarship holders say that change in visa rules delays the start of internships in Spain
articles.summary: Dozens of Brazilian scholarship holders supported by Capes report that a recent change in Spain’s visa rules has delayed the start of their research internships in the country. The delays have led to financial losses, including expenses for insurance and rebooking of travel tickets.
articles.insight:
This incident highlights growing visa policy volatility in key study destinations, potentially amplifying perceptions among Latin American students that bureaucratic hurdles and financial unpredictability are rising—though it remains unclear whether this will materially shift demand toward English-speaking countries or merely heighten pre-application anxiety.  
Admissions teams should track sentiment shifts in Brazilian and broader Latin American social media and agent networks, and consider refreshing visa-preparation resources to proactively address concerns about timeline reliability and cost contingencies for prospective applicants.

articles.title: US: Climate of uncertainty continues for international students amid legal action on internships and a proposed $70,000 OPT fee
articles.summary: In August 2026, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) issued two broadcast memos indicating increased scrutiny of Curricular Practical Training (CPT) placements for international students. The article also notes ongoing uncertainty due to legal action concerning internships and a proposed $70,000 fee for Optional Practical Training (OPT).
articles.insight:
This news signals growing regulatory scrutiny of U.S. work-integrated learning pathways, potentially dampening student interest in U.S. degrees—especially among those prioritising post-study employment—though direct demand impacts remain uncertain pending litigation outcomes and policy finalisation.  
Admissions teams should track ICE guidance updates, OPT fee developments, and comparative policy shifts in the UK, Australia, and New Zealand to assess relative attractiveness and refine messaging around career pathways and visa stability.

articles.title: Slow start: foreign university campuses in India yet to see full intake
articles.summary: Foreign university campuses in India are experiencing a slow start and have yet to achieve full student intake. Annual fees for undergraduate or postgraduate programmes at these institutions range from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh.
articles.insight:
This news suggests potential softening in domestic demand for premium international education within India, possibly reflecting affordability concerns, regulatory uncertainty, or shifting preferences—though it’s too early to confirm whether this signals broader declines in outbound student mobility to traditional destinations.  
Admissions teams should monitor Indian student application and enrolment trends closely over the next 12–18 months, particularly for high-fee programmes, while assessing whether local campus initiatives are diverting aspirational students or merely capturing a niche segment.
